title: Limhi and Ammon address the people
summary: After finishing his speech, Limhi tells his people about their brethren in Zarahemla. He has Ammon stand before the multitude. Ammon recounts what happened to their brethren from Zeniff’s departure until his own arrival, then rehearses and explains King Benjamin’s last words.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi finishes speaking to his people and tells them about their brethren in the land of Zarahemla.
Limhi causes Ammon to stand before the multitude and recount what happened to their brethren from Zeniff’s departure until Ammon’s arrival.
Ammon rehearses King Benjamin’s last words and explains them to Limhi’s people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi’s people are gathered as Ammon stands before them.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and physical appearances are not described.

narration.text: he told his people all the things
he caused that Ammon should stand up
and explained them to the people of king Limhi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon’s account of earlier events is reported speech, not a separate present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Zeniff or King Benjamin as physically present.
Do not invent the words spoken by Limhi or Ammon.

title: The multitude is dismissed
summary: After Ammon finishes, Limhi dismisses the multitude and directs them to return to their homes.

explicit_facts.text: After Ammon finishes, Limhi dismisses the multitude and causes each person to return to their own house.

unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place and the homes' appearance.

narration.text: return every one unto his own house.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific destination or route for any individual.

title: The plates are brought to Ammon
summary: Limhi has his people's record brought before Ammon. After reading it, Ammon is asked whether he can interpret languages and says he cannot.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi has the plates containing his people's record brought before Ammon so Ammon can read them.
After reading the record, Ammon is asked whether he can interpret languages and answers that he cannot.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The record is placed before Ammon, who reads it.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and material of the record's plates; the room and furnishings.

narration.text: the plates which contained the record of his people
as soon as Ammon had read the record

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the plates as the twenty-four gold plates described later; the text distinguishes them.

title: The king recounts the journey
summary: The king tells someone that he sent forty-three of his people into the wilderness to find Zarahemla and seek deliverance from bondage. They were lost for many days, did not find Zarahemla, and returned after traveling among many waters and discovering a land covered with bones and ruins.
characters: An unnamed person addressed by the king

explicit_facts.text: The king says he sent forty-three of his people into the wilderness to find Zarahemla and appeal to their brethren for deliverance from bondage.
The group was lost for many days, did not find Zarahemla, and returned to their land after traveling among many waters.
They discovered a land covered with human and animal bones and ruins of buildings; the king says it had been peopled by a very numerous people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king speaks to another person while recounting an earlier expedition.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers' appearances and the setting of their conversation are not described.
The expedition's route and the discovered land's precise appearance are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Being grieved for the afflictions of my people, I caused that forty and three of my people should take a journey into the wilderness,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king

narration.text: And the king said unto him:
and found not the land of Zarahemla but returned to this land,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The journey and discovery are events the king recounts, not actions occurring during the conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the king or the person he addresses from these verses alone.
Do not stage the earlier expedition as a present-time event.
Do not invent the expedition members' identities or details of the ruined land.

title: The records and the request for translation
summary: An unidentified speaker reports that a group brought engraved gold plates, breastplates, and damaged swords. The speaker recalls an earlier question about translation, asks whether the addressee knows anyone who can translate, and expresses a desire to learn about the destroyed people and the cause of their destruction.

explicit_facts.text: A group brought twenty-four engraved plates of pure gold as testimony that what they had said was true.
The group also brought large, perfectly sound breastplates of brass and copper.
The group brought swords with perished hilts and blades cankered with rust.
The speaker says no one in the land can interpret the language or engravings on the plates and reports having earlier asked the addressee whether they could translate.
The speaker asks whether the addressee knows anyone who can translate and wishes to learn about the people connected with the records and the cause of their destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The artifacts can be illustrated as reported objects without depicting their arrival as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the participants’ appearances.
The plates’ engravings and the artifacts’ precise shapes.

spoken_dialogue.text: Knowest thou of any one that can translate?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

narration.text: they have brought twenty-four plates which are filled with engravings, and they are of pure gold.
they have brought breastplates, which are large, and they are of brass and of copper, and are perfectly sound.
the blades thereof were cankered with rust

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earlier question about translation is reported speech, not a new exchange in this scene.
The destruction is discussed, not depicted as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the speaker, addressee, or group.
Do not depict the people's destruction or invent its cause.
Do not show the reported arrival of the artifacts as a present event.

title: Ammon describes a seer
summary: Ammon tells a king of a man who can translate ancient records, explains the interpreters and the term seer, and identifies the king in Zarahemla as the man commanded to do this.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon tells the king of a man who can translate ancient records and says the interpreters are a gift from God.
Ammon says that a person commanded to look in the interpreters is called a seer.
Ammon identifies the king of the people in Zarahemla as the man commanded to do these things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon speaks to the king he addresses.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearances of Ammon and the king are not described.
The appearance of the interpreters is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: I can assuredly tell thee, O king, of a man that can translate the records;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

spoken_dialogue.text: And the things are called interpreters,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, the king of the people who are in the land of Zarahemla is the man that is commanded to do these things,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The translation and use of the interpreters are described in Ammon's speech, not narrated as occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a translation taking place or the interpreters in use.
Do not depict the king in Zarahemla as physically present or invent an appearance for him.
Do not assign a name to the king Ammon addresses based on these verses alone.

title: Ammon explains the seer's gift
summary: The king says a seer is greater than a prophet. Ammon says a seer is also a revelator and prophet, explains what a seer can know and make known, and says God has provided a means for people to work mighty miracles through faith and benefit others.

explicit_facts.text: The king says a seer is greater than a prophet.
Ammon says a seer is a revelator and a prophet, and that a person may receive great power from God.
Ammon says a seer can know things past and future and make hidden or otherwise unknown things known.
Ammon says God has provided a means for people, through faith, to work mighty miracles and benefit fellow beings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king and Ammon may be shown conversing.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearances, gestures, and surroundings are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: And the king said that a seer is greater than a prophet.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the king

spoken_dialogue.text: And Ammon said that a seer is a revelator and a prophet also;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

narration.text: But a seer can know of things which are past,
Thus God has provided a means that man, through faith, might work mighty miracles;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements about knowledge and miracles are teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a vision, miracle, divine appearance, or revealed event as occurring in this scene.
Do not assign the king a name or specify a location from outside these verses.

title: The king rejoices
summary: After Ammon finishes speaking, the king rejoices, gives thanks to God, speaks of the plates and interpreters, praises the Lord's works, and compares people to a wild flock.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon finishes speaking; the king rejoices exceedingly and gives thanks to God.
The king says a great mystery is contained within the plates and that the interpreters were prepared to unfold mysteries.
The king praises the Lord's works and patience and says people will not seek wisdom.
The king compares people to a wild flock fleeing its shepherd, scattering, and being devoured by forest beasts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king appears joyful as he gives thanks.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, gestures, and whether the plates or interpreters are visible.

spoken_dialogue.text: Doubtless a great mystery is contained within these plates, and these interpreters were doubtless prepared for the purpose of unfolding all such mysteries to the children of men.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the king

spoken_dialogue.text: O how marvelous are the works of the Lord,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the king

narration.text: And now, when Ammon had made an end of speaking these words the king rejoiced exceedingly, and gave thanks to God, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The flock, shepherd, and beasts are a comparison in the king's speech, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal flock, shepherd, or beasts.
